meta.title: Chinchpoklicha Chintamani
meta.location: Chinchpokli East, near the railway station; office on Dattaram Lad Marg, Mumbai
meta.foundedNote: Official history gives foundation 6 September and first installation 16 September 1920; contemporary press corroborates the year.
meta.intro: Chinchpoklicha Chintamani is the festival idol of Chinchpokli Sarvajanik Utsav Mandal, founded in 1920 in the mill district. Its institutional account links the beginning to the weeks after Lokmanya Tilak’s death. A long sculptural repertoire and the Aagman arrival procession shape its public identity. This collection distinguishes the Mumbai institution from later authorized-looking replicas elsewhere, and preserves conflicts within its retrospective artist and anniversary chronology.

paragraphs.text: The official account places foundation on 6 September 1920, with the first idol installed ten days later at Deccan Core. It remembers four-anna subscriptions and a collective early leadership. These specific dates remain institutional retrospective testimony; no original 1920 minutes or photograph were inspected.

sections.title: A permanent base and a wider remit

paragraphs.text: The mandal says it acquired its railway-side home nineteen years after founding, and that a 1956 constitution widened the name to Sarvajanik Utsav Mandal. Navratri began that year too. Its anniversary labels need caution: the official history places the silver jubilee in 1945, while Loksatta’s later account says 1944. Festival-year counting may explain part of the difference, but original programmes are needed.

sections.title: A repertoire built by several hands

paragraphs.text: The institutional sculptor page credits Shyam Sarang’s 1953-1969 work, including a 1953 serpent composition, followed by Weling in 1971-1986 and Vijay Khatu in 1987-2007. It credits Reshma Khatu with the centenary idol. Its implication about Weling’s death conflicts with Ganesh Galli’s final-1990 account; artist assignments and death chronology must be kept separate.

A 2023 report interviews Reshma Khatu about an idol made for a Surat mandal using Chintamani’s signature face but a different body. Those photographs depict the Surat commission, not automatically the Mumbai original. The 2025 Mumbai press image instead shows a royal throne interpretation described as Sambhaji-inspired, demonstrating why identifying an idol requires more than recognizing a face.

The Aagman procession is a major part of the contemporary record. Loksatta’s 2024 report reproduces the mandal’s announcement for 31 August. That supports that year’s event, not a permanent date or route. The original 2019 street photograph provides a separately dated physical scene rather than a decontextualized devotional cutout.

sections.title: Scenes, craft credits and the limits of an archive frame

paragraphs.text: The official retrospective gallery contains eighty-eight framed objects spanning several decades. Its selected monochrome stage photographs show a relaxed throne pose in 1948, a standing shrine in 1951, and elaborate carts, courts and mythological narratives in the 1950 s-1980 s. The modern frame supplies explicit annual labels. It establishes what the institution attributes to each year, while leaving the original negative, print generation and any retouching unresolved.

A 1972 print explicitly credits Dinanath Weling as sculptor, a positive annual record consistent with the institutional biography. Current work needs the same care: 2022 and 2024 reporting names Reshma Khatu, while the 2026 institutional report names Siddhesh Dighole and separately credits scenic, costume and lighting artists. A workshop lineage or familiar face should not be extended across those years without a specific commission record.

notes.text: Official annual report dates patpujan to 25 July and arrival to 29 August 2026. Loksatta's gallery update is 9 September and uses present-tense arrival wording; that publication timestamp is not substituted for the event date.

Separate official credits name Sachin Panchal for decoration, Prakash Lahane for costume and Vishal Shelar for lighting. The annual page also names Avadhoot Hembarde for the photo session and Amar Jadhav for festival photography; those credits are not automatically reassigned to this @best.capture image.

media.caption: Ganesh with disc, conch and upright staff before a Garuda-backed blue throne, surrounded by people photographing the arrival.
media.credit: @best.capture (visible watermark); mandal/Instagram via Loksatta. Personal photographer name not established.
media.dateEvidence: Specific image in Loksatta's 2026 Chintamani arrival gallery, independently matched to the official 2026 form and annual report. Exact capture day not supplied.

visualReview.observedForm: Large four-armed Ganesh with gold crown and jewellery, white drape and maroon ornamented stole; disc, conch and gold staff; sculpted eagle head/wings above a blue throne, lion at left, trees, tarpaulin, people and phones in foreground; @best.capture watermark.
visualReview.note: Direct original individually viewed. Physical street/people and the distinctive Garuda throne match the official 2026 archive form; photograph appearance alone does not establish the year.

openQuestions.title: Weling’s death and exact succession
openQuestions.text: This official page implies an endpoint before 1987, while Ganesh Galli says a final 1990 idol. Seek memorial or contemporary records. Do not alter either account to fit the other.

openQuestions.title: Anniversary dates
openQuestions.text: Silver-jubilee labels differ between 1944 and 1945. Separate inclusive festival-year counting from completed anniversaries and inspect original programmes.

openQuestions.title: Replica identification
openQuestions.text: Related faces appear in other cities. Confirm institution, location and body composition before reusing images as Mumbai Chintamani.

claims.text: Foundation and first installation are dated September 1920 in the institutional history.
1956 brought a broader institutional constitution/name and Navratri according to its history.
Sarang, Weling, Vijay Khatu and Reshma Khatu are named in the mandal’s sculptural history; exact succession is not fully reconciled.
The 2023 Surat idol is a separate related commission, not the Mumbai original.
The 2026 annual report credits Siddhesh Dighole; earlier Reshma Khatu commissions do not establish automatic 2026 authorship.

researchNotes.coverage: Official Marathi history and artist page, regional announcement, contemporary replica interview, two visually inspected documentary photo years. Phase 2 inspected all 88 official archive objects, added eighteen source-labelled historical stage-photo years and current annual craft records through 2026, with 2024 composite classification explicit.
gaps: Archive frame dates remain retrospective attributions; original print backs/negatives and many studio-role credits are unverified.
The 2022 header photo lacks independent capture-year evidence and is not in the dated media sequence.
